references.title: Allan Gibbard, ‘Contingent Identity’ (1975), full text
references.support: Gibbard’s original article. Relevant passages pp. 189–192 give his stipulated persistence criteria, the Goliath/Lumpl setup, and the squeezing counterfactual; pp. 193–194 and 210–211 develop the proposal’s treatment of names and modal predication. The audit checked these passages in a full-text reproduction, not the article cover to cover; this establishes what Gibbard argues, not that the disputed conclusion is correct.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Material Constitution
references.support: Ryan Wasserman’s scholarly reference entry, relevant passages in the Spring 2024 archive: §1 outlines the statue-and-clay puzzle and prominent replies; §2 discusses coinciding objects and the grounding challenge. Context for competing approaches, not a claim that one solution is settled.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Identity
references.support: Harold Noonan and Ben Curtis, SEP Identity §7, relevant passage read in the current entry: summarizes Gibbard’s example, the response of denying identity, related person/body cases, and the continuing controversy about contingent-identity arguments. Scholarly synthesis, not a settled verdict.

references.title: Wolfgang Schwarz, ‘Contingent Identity’ (2013)
references.support: Peer-reviewed survey in Philosophy Compass 8(5), 486–495. Relevant sections of the full-text repository copy (§§2–4) discuss Gibbard’s case, objections including Leibniz’s Law, and accounts of contingent identity and modal predication. Survey evidence for the live debate, not a consensus claim.
